Author: @diablogaming9429
Content:
Guga!! Hey Nice video!!
Did you know the Salvadorian Home Food?, I would like you to try to make, replicate or improve my family's recipe for a good breakfast, be careful everything has to be homemade you can't buy anything prepared or precooked.
The recipe is called "Tomatada", as the name says it is basically a kind of non-liquefied tomato sauce, and it is very easy to make but it requires a lot of time (maximum 4 hours of preparation) that is why when we prepare it we get up very early in the morning, or we leave some ingredients ready the night before.
The ingredients are:
10 tomatoes.
4 onions (2 white and 2 purple).
1 chicken or beef flavored broth.
1 pound of beans of your preference (either red or black), you must prepare these the night before, since in the morning the only thing you will do is blend them and cook them.
2 Eggs or more depending on the number of diners at breakfast
2 Bananas
and
Cream or Cheese of your choice (if you choose the cheese, I recommend CU-AJA-DA, a typical cheese from my country that is creamy but at the same time consistent with a light and pleasant flavor).
2 loaves of bread (since you won't want to use cutlery, just your hands to eat it).

The preparation is as follows:
For the sauce, boil the tomatoes until they break their skin or become very soft (I estimate that depending on the heat of the flame they will be ready in 10 or 15 minutes on high heat, but for better consistency we prefer to cook them on low heat), after removing them from the heat you have to peel them, that is, remove the skin, and immediately mash them by hand with a fork (do not use machinery to mash them since blenders and food processors leave the tomato very liquid and mushy, we do not want that), then set aside the sauce and start cutting the onion into slices, then in a frying pan or semi-deep pot add 1 splash of cooking oil, sauté the onion until it changes color (without overcooking it, it should be crispy), then add the crushed tomato, season it with the broth and adjust the seasoning with a pinch of salt, let it boil for a few minutes and then remove it from the heat.
Now with the eggs you just have to make them fried, not scrambled, as if you were going to add them to a hamburger on top of the meat, the yolk should be liquid or, failing that, semi-cooked.
For the bananas it's simple, fry them in slices (they should be caramelized, not dry or burnt).
Now for the beans: you must clean them first before cooking them (some packaged ones are not well cleaned of stones, pebbles, dust or dry leaves), then in a large soup pot you must add the beans with plenty of water, you will know that it is enough when the bean seeds are completely submerged in the water, add the previously peeled garlic cloves, then boil them and season them with salt and pepper, (be careful not to add too much salt or pepper because while they are boiling you will have to add water to the soup several times, you do not want them to dry out, so you can rectify the flavor to your liking) then let them boil until most of the beans are soft, then remove them from the heat and set aside, in the morning blend them (do not worry if they remain liquid) then add 1 splash of oil to the pot or pan, add the blended beans and boil them for a few minutes (10-20 minutes max) over medium heat, then remove them and Let them rest.
When serving, the order is this:
first the eggs, then you serve the blended beans on one side of the egg, then you serve the plantain on the other side of the egg, you serve the tomato sauce on top of the eggs (they should be covered by the sauce), serve the bread and cheese to your liking, and that's it, your breakfast is ready.
I hope you enjoy it, believe me, it's worth making.😅😅😅
